messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.series_name
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS k
  ON k.Channel = c.id
ORDER BY c.series_name;
```
I think you need to find out which countries these tv channels are from.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.Country,
  c.id AS channel_id,
  c.series_name AS channel_name
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS k
  ON k.Channel = c.id
ORDER BY c.Country, c.series_name;
```
You also need to check if these channels are currently airing the cartoons.

The schema doesn’t include any “currently airing” flag or an end date/time for cartoons—only `Cartoon.Original_air_date` (first air date). If you mean “channels that have aired cartoons at least once”, that’s what the previous query does.

If you want “currently airing” defined as “has aired a cartoon on/after a cutoff date”, you can do:

```sql
-- Replace :cutoff_date with e.g. '2024-01-01'
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.Country,
  c.id AS channel_id,
  c.series_name AS channel_name
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS k
  ON k.Channel = c.id
WHERE date(k.Original_air_date) >= date(:cutoff_date)
ORDER BY c.Country, c.series_name;
```

Tell me how you want to define “currently airing” (e.g., last 30 days, since a specific date, or based on another table/field), and what date format `Original_air_date` uses in your data.
Also need to check if the cartoons are by Todd Casey.

```sql
-- Channels (with country) that are airing/has-aired cartoons by Todd Casey
-- If you need "currently airing", add a date filter on Original_air_date (see below).
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.Country,
  c.id   AS channel_id,
  c.series_name AS channel_name
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS k
  ON k.Channel = c.id
WHERE k.Directed_by = 'Todd Casey'
   OR k.Written_by  = 'Todd Casey'
ORDER BY c.Country, c.series_name;
```

If you want “currently airing” as “aired since a cutoff date”:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.Country,
  c.id   AS channel_id,
  c.series_name AS channel_name
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS k
  ON k.Channel = c.id
WHERE (k.Directed_by = 'Todd Casey' OR k.Written_by = 'Todd Casey')
  AND date(k.Original_air_date) >= date(:cutoff_date);  -- e.g. '2024-01-01'
```
